question: In the periodic table, what is the trend for atomic radius as you move from left to right across a period (horizontal row)?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Atomic radius decreases**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• As you move from left to right across a period in the periodic table, atomic radius decreases.
 
• This decrease is due to the increase in nuclear charge (number of protons) which pulls electrons closer to the nucleus.
 
• Despite the addition of more electrons, they are added to the same energy level, resulting in a stronger attraction between the nucleus and the electrons.
 
• The increased effective nuclear charge reduces the size of the electron cloud, thereby decreasing the atomic radius.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Effective Nuclear Charge (Z_eff)**: The net positive charge experienced by an electron in a multi-electron atom, influencing atomic size.
 
• **Shielding Effect**: Electrons in inner shells can shield outer electrons from the full charge of the nucleus, but across a period, the shielding effect does not increase significantly.
 
• **Ionic Radius**: The radius of an atom's ion. Cations (positively charged ions) are smaller than their neutral atoms, while anions (negatively charged ions) are larger.
 
• **Periodic Trends**: Periodic trends are patterns in the periodic table that show the variation in certain properties, such as atomic radius, ionization energy, and electronegativity.
 
• **Atomic Radius Measurement**: Atomic radius is typically measured in picometers (pm) or angstroms (Å), where 1 Å = 100 pm.
